title: On Allowing nobody to leave early
subtitle: 法律规则 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 法律规则（社会服务与人际沟通·法律与规则）
meta: 主题语境：法律规则（社会服务与人际沟通·法律与规则）　|　核心词汇：allow　|　正文 352 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 allow 的形式与含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1969 the baker ① allowed nobody to leave early for the whole place, and every customer in the bakery said it was the first time anybody had done such a thing there. Three weeks on, people still spoke of how quietly it was done and of how, ever since, the baker ② allows nobody to leave early without a word of thanks without being asked. My mother said later that to ③ allow nobody to leave early at all was the part nobody had expected.

By then somebody had surely ④ allowed nobody to leave early before — a line in the bill for December 1963 hints at it — but nobody could name the person. ⑤ Allowing nobody to leave early for the whole place, the baker said once, is nine parts patience and one part nerve; it is not the doing of it that people remember.

My uncle, who kept the tray at the far oven, meant the other thing entirely. He said that if anybody should ever ⑥ allow an hour for the whole walk without a word of thanks, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again. The rule the old hands handed down was plainer still: ⑦ Allow an hour for the whole walk at once and never mention it again.

By 1976 the whole business had shrunk to half a line in the bill, and a new customer from the next bakery ⑧ allows an hour for the whole walk for the whole place every week without once asking what it had cost the first time. My mother, who had watched all of it from the oven, said nothing at all; she simply ⑨ allowed nobody to leave early again when nobody else would.

⑩ To allow nobody to leave early, my mother said in 1981, is not one thing but two: what you do and what the bakery remembers of it. She said the second half never grows lighter, and nowadays, whenever the bakery forgets, somebody allows nobody to leave early without a word of thanks again and somebody must allow nobody to leave early for the whole place all over again.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请为文中十处画线形式选择对应的用法说明。
options: A. v. 允许（一般过去式 allowed nobody to leave early：1969 年面点师头一回这样做，替所有人）
B. v. 允许（一般现在 allows nobody to leave early：自那以后成了老习惯，不必有人开口）
C. v. 允许（不定式 to allow nobody to leave early：文中两处，一是母亲说的“难就难在……”，一是结尾那句格言）
D. v. 允许（过去完成时 had allowed nobody to leave early：1963 年十二月的账单上那行字之前就有人做过）
E. v. 允许（动名词 allowing nobody to leave early 作主语：“九分耐心、一分胆气”那一句）
F. v. 留出（allow an hour for the whole walk：should ever 之后的原形，指万一真要去留出整趟路留出的一个钟头）
G. v. 留出（allow an hour for the whole walk：祈使句，转述老手们当年立下的那条规矩）
H. v. 允许（后段两处：新来的顾客照例 allows an hour for the whole walk，而母亲又一次 allowed nobody to leave early）

items.q: to allow nobody to leave early
allowed nobody to leave early before
allow an hour for the whole walk without a word of thanks
allow an hour for the whole walk at once
allows an hour for the whole walk for the whole place

to allow nobody to leave early

answers.why: allow 意为“允许”，1969 年面点师替所有人允许不许任何人早走，那是糕饼铺里头一回有人肯这么做，故用一般过去式 allowed。
allow 意为“允许”，自那以后面点师不图一句谢把这件事做了一遍又一遍，不必有人开口，故用一般现在 allows。
allow 意为“允许”，母亲说的是“难就难在肯允许不许任何人早走”，此处为不定式 to allow nobody to leave early。
allow 意为“允许”，账单里 十二月 那行字说明早在 1976 年之前就有人允许过，故用过去完成时 had allowed。
allow 意为“允许”，面点师说“允许不许任何人早走这件事是九分耐心一分胆气”，此处 allowing nobody to leave early 作主语。
allow 意为“留出”，叔叔说的是“万一真有人去留出整趟路留出的一个钟头”，should ever 之后用原形 allow an hour for the whole walk。
allow 意为“留出”，老手们留下的规矩是祈使句：立刻留出整趟路留出的一个钟头（allow an hour for the whole walk at once），以后再也不要提起。
allow 意为“允许”，新来的顾客每个星期都照例留出整趟路留出的一个钟头，从不问头一回的代价，用一般现在 allows。
allow 意为“允许”，母亲在无人肯做的时候又一次替所有人允许不许任何人早走，用一般过去式 allowed 叙述。
allow 意为“允许”，结尾那句是母亲 1981 年的话：要允许不许任何人早走，其实不是一件事，而是两件事——你做的那一件，和糕饼铺记住的那一件。

task3.title: Task 3　语境写作
task3.intro: 请写 5—6 个句子，至少使用 allow 的 3 种不同形式（过去式、第三人称、-ing、不定式等）；至少使用下列词语中的 3 个。
answers: In 1969 the baker allowed nobody to leave early for the whole place, and nobody in the bakery forgot it.
Even now the baker allows nobody to leave early without a word of thanks whenever the bakery asks.
Allowing nobody to leave early for the whole place, my mother used to say, is nine parts patience and one part nerve.
If anybody should ever allow an hour for the whole walk without a word of thanks, nobody should do it twice or speak of it again.
A new customer from the next bakery allows an hour for the whole walk for the whole place every week, asking nothing about the past.
When nobody else would, my mother allowed nobody to leave early again, and the bakery remembered that half.
